questions.title: Which Russian official will the Kremlin publicly confirm as attending Ali Khamenei's state funeral?
questions.background: Iran's supreme leader Ali Khamenei was killed on February 28, 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the Russian official whose planned attendance at Ali Khamenei's state funeral is publicly confirmed by the Kremlin. Use the Kremlin's announcement or reliable reporting of it. This question concerns the announcement, not actual attendance. Resolution Date : 2026-07-02 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the official's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Iran rescheduled Ali Khamenei's state funeral to July 4-9, 2026, and President Pezeshkian only began issuing foreign invitations around June 23-24. Strong precedent favors State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin, whom the Kremlin sent to lead Russia's delegations to both Ebrahim Raisi's funeral (May 2024) and Pezeshkian's inauguration (July 2024), while Vladimir Putin is very unlikely to travel to Tehran shortly after a four-month air war. Because Khamenei was Supreme Leader and heads of government like Pakistan's PM are expected, Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, Federation Council Chairwoman Valentina Matviyenko, and Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu are the main alternatives, leaving 16% tail mass on Putin, Dmitry Medvedev, Alexander Novak, or other envoys.

questions.title: Which month will the Palestinian Football Association announce for the resumption of its football competitions after their October 2023 suspension?
questions.background: Palestinian football competitions have been suspended since the war in Gaza began in October 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Palestinian Football Association announcement, or reliable news reporting quoting its leadership. Resolution Conditions : Use the first public announcement between July 1 and August 31, 2026, that specifies a date for restarting the suspended football competitions. Resolve to the calendar month containing that announced restart date, regardless of whether competitions subsequently begin as scheduled. If no qualifying announcement occurs by the deadline, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The full English name of the month, not the month in which the announcement is made.
questions.current_reasoning: Gaza hosted a PFA-supervised 5-a-side recovery tournament in Feb–Mar 2026 following the Oct 2025 ceasefire, while Al Jazeera reported on June 14, 2026 that the West Bank / Palestine Professional League remains suspended with hopes of a scaled-down revival 'after the summer break concludes.' Historically the Palestinian domestic season begins in late August or September, and an announcement made between July 1 and August 31 would typically allow 4–8 weeks of lead time for squad registration and logistics. Conditioning on a qualifying announcement, September (0.33), August (0.23), and October (0.22) capture the core window, with November (0.09), July (0.06), and a 7% tail for December or later.

questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: On June 23, 2026, Oman and Iran issued an official bilateral joint statement during Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and FM Araghchi's visit to Muscat, establishing a joint working group on Strait of Hormuz navigation and maritime services directly under Clause 5 of the June 18 Islamabad MoU (which also obligates Iran to conduct mine-clearing within 30 days). As co-coastal state of the Strait of Hormuz already operating an IMO-coordinated corridor, Oman is the clear favorite for a bilateral joint mine-clearance project with Iran, whereas Britain and France are pursuing a separate Western coalition without bilateral Iranian agreement. China (Iran's top oil customer with advanced demining capability), Japan (which Al Jazeera reported on June 24 is actively weighing deploying minesweepers to Hormuz and enjoys uniquely cordial Tehran ties), Russia (Iran's strategic naval partner), and Pakistan (mediator of the Islamabad MoU with minehunters) are the main alternatives, leaving 15% tail mass for the US, UAE, Turkey, India, or others.

local_articles.title: How minesweeping in the Strait of Hormuz works: A visual guide
local_articles.snippet: Last week, the United States and Iran signed a framework agreement aimed at ending the US-Israel war on Iran and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Navigation through the strait, a global energy chokepoint, has picked up since then, but experts said it will take some time for shipping traffic to return to levels seen before the war began on February 28. Shipping companies and insurers have warned that the strait remains highly dangerous, largely because of fears of sea mines. The warnings follow threats made early in the conflict by Iran, which said various types of naval mines were at its disposal to block the passage of ships through the waterway. While Iran threatened to deploy naval mines, it did not comment on whether its forces had actually planted them. questions.title: Which UK party leader will announce plans in early July 2026 to resign as an MP and contest the resulting by-election?
questions.background: A parliamentary resignation can trigger a by-election, which the departing MP may contest to seek a fresh mandate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public announcements corroborated by contemporaneous reporting from BBC News, The Guardian, or Al Jazeera. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the UK political party leader who publicly announces, between July 1 and July 9, 2026, plans to resign from the House of Commons and stand in the by-election caused by that resignation. The announcement is sufficient; the by-election need not have taken place. Accepted Answer Format : The party leader's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Rupert Lowe (Restore Britain leader, MP for Great Yarmouth) uniquely fits both historical UK precedents for an MP resigning to contest a by-election: he was elected under Reform UK in 2024 before launching Restore Britain in Feb 2026 (which just finished 3rd in Makerfield with ~7%), and on May 15, 2026 he lost his High Court challenge to halt a parliamentary ICGS watchdog probe, creating strong incentive to seek a fresh mandate or preempt a suspension/recall petition. Very few UK party leaders sit in the Commons; Nigel Farage (Reform UK), Jeremy Corbyn (Your Party, elected Independent), Zarah Sultana (ex-Labour/Your Party), and Kemi Badenoch represent smaller tails, with ~12% left for other minor-party MP leaders (e.g., Northern Ireland party leaders or a newly formed breakaway party).

questions.title: Who will Moldova’s parliament elect as prime minister to succeed Alexandru Munteanu?
questions.background: Alexandru Munteanu has resigned as Moldova’s prime minister, triggering his cabinet’s resignation. Moldova is pursuing European Union membership.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Moldovan parliamentary announcements or reliable news reporting confirming the election of a new prime minister. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first person elected prime minister by Moldova’s parliament following Alexandru Munteanu’s resignation. A nomination or temporary appointment as acting prime minister does not qualify. Resolution Date : The date parliament elects the successor. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the person elected.
questions.current_reasoning: Moldova's pro-EU ruling party PAS holds a 55/101 parliamentary majority alongside President Maia Sandu, so the successor to PM Alexandru Munteanu (whose Control Corps resigned over loss of trust on June 24, 2026) will be a PAS-backed pick. Top internal cabinet/party contenders are Deputy PM & Foreign Minister Mihai Popșoi, Deputy PM for European Integration Cristina Gherasimov (aligned with the EU accession priority), PAS leader and Speaker Igor Grosu, Deputy PM Vladimir Bolea, and Deputy PM for Economic Development Eugen Osmochescu. Because Sandu and PAS have a strong base rate of tapping surprise technocrats or presidential advisers (as with Dorin Recean in 2023 and Munteanu in Nov 2025), 42% probability mass is left outside the top five.

questions.title: Which Indian cricketer will publicly say by September 20, 2026, that the 2027 men's ODI World Cup will be his last for India?
questions.background: The men's ODI World Cup is the global championship for cricket's 50-over international format.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : A public statement or interview by the player, quoted by a reputable news organization. Resolution Condition : Identify the Indian cricketer who publicly declares between September 1 and September 20, 2026, inclusive, that the 2027 men's ODI World Cup will be his final World Cup representing India. The question resolves when the declaration is made, not when the player subsequently retires. Accepted Answer Format : The player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: As of June 2026, both Rohit Sharma (39, turning 40 before the Oct-Nov 2027 World Cup) and Virat Kohli (37, turning 38 in November) have retired from Tests and T20Is to play exclusively ODIs, with constant Indian media scrutiny (including Ashwin, Manjrekar, and Saba Karim in June 2026) framing 2027 as their definitive swansong. Because neither could realistically play the 2031 edition, Rohit (43%, older, recently replaced as captain by Shubman Gill, and candid in interviews) and Kohli (36%, locked into India's 2027 plans and already addressing 2027 questions publicly) account for nearly 80% of probability mass. Fellow 37-year-old T20I retiree Ravindra Jadeja (8%), fast bowler Mohammed Shami (6%, turning 36 on September 3 during the window), and 34-year-old ODI regular KL Rahul (3%) are the main secondary contenders.

questions.title: Who will be appointed to succeed Pape Thiaw as head coach of Senegal's men's national football team by August 31, 2026?
questions.background: The Senegalese Football Federation is responsible for appointing the national team's head coach.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by the Senegalese Football Federation, as confirmed by contemporaneous reliable news reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the person publicly announced as Pape Thiaw's successor between August 1 and August 31, 2026. The resolution date is the date the appointment is publicly announced, rather than the coach's presentation or first match. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Despite signing a belated contract extension on June 21 after months of friction with the FSF and a five-match CAF ban from the controversial Jan 2026 AFCON final, Pape Thiaw is under severe pressure with Senegal 0–2 at World Cup 2026 (losses to France and Norway). Conditioning on an August 2026 replacement announcement with no shortlist yet formed, the FSF has strongly favored former Senegalese internationals and internal youth-title winners (Habib Beye, Omar Daf, Malick Daf) or proven Francophone African specialists (Hervé Renard), alongside a possible return for former champion Aliou Cissé. Given high pre-vacancy candidate entropy across 15+ plausible Senegalese and French coaches, these top five sum conservatively to 43%.
